subclass: Multi-Period Factory Production, Sales, and Inventory Planning
reference: Pochet, Yves, and Laurence A. Wolsey. Production Planning by Mixed Integer Programming. Springer Series in Operations Research and Financial Engineering (2006).
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
Let T be planning periods, P products, and M machine types. Continuous variables Production[t,p], Sales[t,p], and Inventory[t,p] represent units manufactured, sold, and held at the end of each period. Maximize total sales revenue sum_{t,p} profit[p] Sales[t,p] minus inventory holding cost sum_{t,p} h Inventory[t,p]. Initial balance requires Production[0,p] = Sales[0,p] + Inventory[0,p]. For later periods, Inventory[t-1,p] + Production[t,p] = Sales[t,p] + Inventory[t,p]. Machine capacity requires sum_p machine_time[m,p] Production[t,p] <= available_machine_hours[t,m] for every period and machine. Sales and inventory are bounded by Sales[t,p] <= sales_limit[t,p] and Inventory[t,p] <= max_inventory. The final period must satisfy Inventory[last,p] = target_inventory[p].
natural_language_example: A factory plans production, sales, and ending inventory for several products over multiple periods. Each product has a profit per unit sold. Each machine type has limited available hours in each period after maintenance, and every product consumes machine hours on each machine type. Sales are capped separately for every product and period. Inventory has a per-unit holding cost, an upper bound, and a required final target for every product. The goal is to maximize sales profit minus inventory holding cost while preserving period-by-period inventory balance, machine-hour capacity, sales upper bounds, inventory bounds, and final stock targets.
local_modification_notes: Internal OR-CPT version exposes all product, period, machine, processing-time, available-hour, sales-limit, inventory-bound, and final-inventory tables, adds compact_factory_planning_tables for LLM-facing prompts, and explicitly forbids unconstrained product-mix or inferred-demand reinterpretations.
